title: Routh's Theorem: Area Ratio for General Cevian Parameters
description: Proves Routh's theorem for arbitrary cevian parameters d, e, f ∈ (0,1): the area of the inner triangle formed by pairwise intersections of the three cevians equals routhRatio(d,e,f) × area(ABC), where routhRatio = (def - (1-d)(1-e)(1-f))² / ((1-e+de)(1-f+ef)(1-d+fd)). Extends the specific 1/3 case from OQ-01 to the complete general formula.

overview.historicalContext: Routh's theorem (1896) generalizes the medial triangle result (area ratio 1/7 for d=e=f=1/3). The general formula gives the area of the inner triangle for any cevian parameters, and reduces to 0 exactly when the Ceva condition holds (concurrent cevians). This file completes the gallery's treatment of cevian geometry by proving the full formula.
overview.problemStatement: For a triangle ABC with cevian points D on BC, E on CA, F on AB (parametrized by d, e, f ∈ (0,1)), what is the area of the inner triangle formed by the pairwise intersections of AD, BE, CF?
overview.text: The area ratio equals (d·e·f - (1-d)·(1-e)·(1-f))² / ((1-e+de)·(1-f+ef)·(1-d+fd)). The proof computes the three intersection points explicitly, establishes the algebraic identity via field_simp+ring, and transfers to general triangles by affine invariance.
overview.proofStrategy: For the standard triangle (A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(0,1)): compute P₁₂=AD∩BE using the existing cevaConcurrencyPoint, define P₂₃=BE∩CF and P₃₁=CF∩AD analogously. Prove signedArea(P₁₂,P₂₃,P₃₁) = routhRatio via field_simp+ring (a polynomial identity in d,e,f). Transfer to general triangles using affine_signedArea and stdToTriangle_det.
keyInsights: The three intersection points are rational functions of d,e,f with denominators w₁=1-e+de, w₂=1-f+ef, w₃=1-d+fd (all positive on (0,1)²)
After clearing denominators, the Routh identity reduces to a polynomial equality proved by ring
Affine maps scale signed area by their determinant: signedArea(M(P), M(Q), M(R)) = M.det × signedArea(P,Q,R)
The result is 0 exactly when def = (1-d)(1-e)(1-f) (Ceva condition = concurrency)
prerequisites: CevasTheoremOQ01: routhRatio, signedArea, cevaConcurrencyPoint, w_pos, stdToTriangle

sections.title: Pairwise Cevian Intersections
sections.summary: Defines cevaBECF (BE∩CF) and cevaCFAD (CF∩AD) for the standard triangle, complementing the existing cevaConcurrencyPoint (AD∩BE).

sections.title: Routh's Theorem for the Standard Triangle
sections.summary: Proves signedArea(P₁₂, P₂₃, P₃₁) = routhRatio d e f for A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(0,1) via field_simp+ring.

sections.title: Affine Invariance and General Triangle
sections.summary: Proves affine_signedArea (area scaling) and transfers the standard triangle result to arbitrary non-degenerate triangles.

sections.title: Concrete Instantiations
sections.summary: Proves specific cases: d=e=f=1/3 gives 1/7 (recovering routh_medial_thirds), d=e=f=2/3 also gives 1/7. Proves degeneracy iff Ceva condition.

conclusion.summary: Routh's theorem is completely proved for all d, e, f ∈ (0,1). The area ratio formula is a rational function of the cevian parameters, always non-negative, equal to 0 exactly when the cevians are concurrent.
conclusion.implications: This completes the gallery's cevian geometry trilogy: Ceva's theorem (concurrency condition), its converse, and now Routh's theorem (area measurement). Any further questions about triangle cevians can be answered using this framework.
openQuestions: Can the Routh formula be extended to non-standard parametrizations (e.g., where D is outside segment BC)?
Is there a higher-dimensional analogue: given a simplex and cevian-like hyperplanes, what is the volume of the inner simplex?
